page.layout: One column of running text, with a woodcut initial at the start of the first paragraph. Page number at top left, running head at top centre. Head "CONCIO LVIII" with "Tit. 2." below it, both centred. No margin notes or footnotes.

main_text.p: stum, pium ac jucundum sit. Reverentia hospitis, qui præsens est, & nos alit perpetuò, retineat in officio & disciplina sanƈta. Idem nobis adsit sua gratia, suoque spiritu, ut possimus omnia, sive edamus, sive bibamus, sive matrimonium contrahamus, sive quid faciamus, in gloriam ejus facere, per Christum Jesum Dominum nostrum. Amen.
main_text.head: CONCIO LVIII
Tit. 2.
main_text.p: Tu vero loquere quæ decent sanam doctrinam. Senes ut sobrii sint, graves, modesti, sanæ fide, charitate, patientia. Anus itidem, ut in habitu sint qui religionem deceat, non calumniatrices, vino multo servientes, ut honesta doceant, quæ possint modestas reddere adolescentulas, ut maritos suos diligant, ut liberos ament, ut sobriæ sint, pura, domus custodes, bonæ, subditæ suis viris, ne sermo Dei male audiat. Adolescentes similiter adhortare, ut sobrii sint, per omnia temetipsum præbens formam bonorum operum in doctrina, integritatem, gravitatem, sermonem sanum, irreprehensibi-lem:

page.notes: Page number printed as "44º" with a raised o; read as 440 in the running text. The woodcut initial is decorative and reads as T, joined to "u" of "Tu". Small ornamental marks stand before "Anus" and "Adolescentes" and after "adhortare"; they are not letters and were left out, except that the mark after "adhortare" may be a printed abbreviation sign, which I have not reproduced. The paragraph is kept as one unbroken paragraph, since the lines run to the margin without indents.
